title: Inertia and internal energy: response at λ = 0 and averaged response

key_results.statement: The inverse inertia $\mu$ of (20.10) of 03-ilang-space/20-cost-and-mass is the coefficient of $F$ in $a(0)$ for a uniform gradient added to any diagonal of $C_b$, and for every product start.
For a body with internal labels, the edge costs summed over the internal labels are $L_{xx'}(0)=2\operatorname{Re}\langle\phi_x\vert T_{xx'}\vert\phi_{x'}\rangle$.
$\mu=-\sum_{\{x,x'\},x\neq x'}L_{xx'}(0)\,\Delta_{xx'}\,g(\Delta_{xx'},\cdot)$; edges between places with the same $x$ do not contribute.

Decoupled body with start $\phi_X\otimes\eta$: $\mu=-\sum_{\{x,x'\},x\neq x'}2\operatorname{Re}[t_{xx'}\phi_X(x)^*\phi_X(x')]\,\Delta_{xx'}\,g(\Delta_{xx'},\cdot)$, independent of $\eta$ and of all on-site blocks $T_{xx}$, uniform or position-dependent.
Model D: the rest cost of clock level $k$ is $M_k=m+d_k=m+2\pi k/(N\lambda_0)$, the gap between the branches is $2M_k$, and $\omega_k''(0)=\tau^2/M_k$.

Model D, start $\phi_X\otimes\lvert1\rangle\otimes\lvert f_k\rangle$: $L_{(x,1,a)(x,1,a')}(0)=-\frac{2\pi}{N^2\lambda_0}\lvert\phi_X(x)\rvert^2\sin((2k+1)\pi n/N)/\sin(\pi n/N)$ with $n=a-a'$, and $L_{hh'}(0)=0$ on all other edges.
Model D, start $\phi_X\otimes\lvert1\rangle\otimes\lvert f_k\rangle$: the inverse inertia of (20.10) is $\mu=0$ for every $\phi_X$, $k$, $N$, $\tau$, $m$, $\kappa$.
Model D at first order in $F$, weak records, start concentrated at $p_0=0$ in the positive branch: $a(\lambda)=\frac{2\tau^2}{M_k}\sin^2(M_k\lambda)\,\kappa^2 g(e,F)\,e$ at every fixed $\lambda$.

Exact for every interval $[\lambda_1,T]$, $T=\lambda_1+\Lambda$: at first order in $F$ and leading order in $\kappa$ the coefficient of $F$ in $\overline a$ is $\frac{\tau^2}{M_k}(1-\rho)\kappa^2\,e\,g(e,\cdot)$ with $\rho=[\sin(2M_kT)-\sin(2M_k\lambda_1)]/(2M_k\Lambda)$ and $\lvert\rho\rvert\le 1/(M_k\Lambda)$.

The average over $[\lambda_1,T]$ is $\overline a=\frac{\tau^2}{M_k}\kappa^2 g(e,F)\,e+\frac{\tau^2}{M_k}\kappa\,\mathcal E\,e$ with the additive error $\mathcal E$ bounded by (6.26), for intervals with $1/(2M_k)\ll\Lambda$ and $\mathcal F_{\max}T\ll\min(1,M_k/\tau)$.

Exact for the two-level problem with force $f$, started in the positive branch at label 0, while $\lvert f\rvert\lambda\le\pi/2$: $\lvert\dot{\bar m}_f(\lambda)-\omega_k'(f\lambda)\rvert\le\frac{\lvert f\rvert\tau^2}{M_k^2}\bigl(1+\frac{\lvert f\rvert\tau}{2M_k^2}\bigr)$.

Exact for every $0\le\lambda_1<T$ with $\mathcal F_{\max}T\le\pi/2$: $\lvert\mathcal E\rvert\le\Gamma_kT^2\Sigma_3+\frac{2}{M_k\Lambda}\bigl(\Sigma_1+\frac{\tau}{2M_k^2}\Sigma_2\bigr)$ with $\Sigma_j=\sum_\xi w_\xi\lvert\mathcal F_\xi\rvert^j$ and $\Gamma_k=2+3\tau^2/(2M_k^2)$.

Order estimate under both conditions of (6.14): $\mathcal E=-\rho\mathcal F+\mathcal N$ with $\mathcal N=O(\Gamma_kT^2\Sigma_3)+O\bigl(\frac{1}{M_k\Lambda}\sum_\xi w_\xi\lvert\mathcal F_\xi\rvert\min\{1,\tau^2\mathcal F_\xi^2T^3/M_k\}\bigr)$; the second term is the accumulated interbranch phase at the ends of the interval and dominates on late intervals.

Averaged inverse inertia of Model D at clock level $k$, the coefficient of $F$ at first order in $F$, leading order in $\kappa$, in the long-interval limit, for every $\lambda_1$: $\mu_{\rm av}(k)=\frac{\tau^2}{m+d_k}\kappa^2\,e\,g(e,\cdot)$.
$M_k\,\mu_{\rm av}(k)=\tau^2\kappa^2\,e\,g(e,\cdot)$ for every $k$: the averaged inverse inertia is inversely proportional to the rest cost, and $M_k/\tau^2=m/\tau^2+2\pi k/(N\lambda_0\tau^2)$.

With $n=e/\sigma_X$: $\mu_{\rm av}(k)=I_k^{-1}\,n\,g(n,\cdot)$, with the background inertia $I_k=M_k/(\tau^2\kappa^2\sigma_X^2)$ and the label inertia $I_k^{\rm lab}=M_k/\tau^2$; the clock cost $d_k$ adds to each like $m$.

Decoupled chain body with arbitrary on-site blocks: $\hat v=\omega'(\hat p)\otimes\mathbb 1_N$ and $\ddot{\hat x}=\mathcal F\omega''(\hat p)+\hat a_{\rm free}$ with $\hat a_{\rm free}=\sum_x(t\lvert x+1\rangle\langle x\rvert+t^*\lvert x\rangle\langle x+1\rvert)\otimes(T_{x+1,x+1}-T_{xx})$, which vanishes iff the on-site blocks are the same at every position.

Decoupled chain body with uniform on-site blocks $T_{xx}=D'$: $\mu_{\rm av}=\mu=\kappa^2\langle\phi_X\vert\omega''(\hat p)\vert\phi_X\rangle\,e\,g(e,\cdot)$, independent of the clock level, of $\eta$ and of $D'$.

Body E, a decoupled body with $t=-i\tau/2$ and position-dependent on-site blocks $T_{xx}=(-1)^x(m\mathbb 1_N+D)$, start on even sites at clock level $k$: $\mu=0$ and $\mu_{\rm av}(k)=\frac{\tau^2}{m+d_k}\kappa^2\,e\,g(e,\cdot)\neq\mu$.

$\mu$ and $\mu_{\rm av}$ coincide for the decoupled body with on-site blocks that are the same at every position; they differ for Model D and for body E, where $\mu=0\neq\mu_{\rm av}(k)$; for position-dependent on-site blocks there is no general relation.

open_issues: A ticking clock (superposition of clock levels) is not treated; the averaged response is the level-weighted mean of (6.15), and whether this mixture is the inertia of one body is open.

(6.26) is exact but not sharp (its endpoint term carries twice the first-order amplitude) and (6.27) is an order estimate without constants; neither controls derivatives with respect to F at finite κ; both hold for the concentrated start after limit 2, and finite-packet corrections and wide packets are not treated.
No statement is made for F_max·T > π/2 (Bloch oscillation) or for F_max·τ ≳ M_k² (branch transitions), where (6.25) is not useful.

Position-dependent on-site blocks: only scalar differences, common eigenvectors and body E are solved; which blocks make the averaged inverse inertia depend on the clock level is not classified, and a general member of the class has no gap that fixes the averaging interval.
Second order in κ (decoherence by the records, the record-induced acceleration at F = 0) is only bounded by (6.26) and estimated by (6.27), not computed.
The meaning of τ and of d₁τ as speeds, and of the inertias (6.20), belongs to criteria 4 and 6 and is outside this package.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions of the acceleration, of the label inertia, of the background response and of every term of the bound (6.26), and the limit τ → 0 in which (6.13), (6.15) and the bound (6.25) vanish.
λ = 0 by an independent route: the acceleration operator (6.12) gives a(0) = 0 for every F on the item-2 start, in agreement with μ = 0 of (6.10) from edge costs; (6.21) gives the same for body E.

The exact bounds (6.25) and (6.26) against the first-order solution (which uses half of each bound), against the secular accumulated-phase term (which fits into the other half exactly while the phase expansion is valid), and against a short interval at the start, where the average tends to a(0) = 0.
